title: Streptavidin dot blot with aptamers
author: Manuela De Las Casas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6gyhbxw

steps.title: Prepare the wax circle
steps.instruction: Create a wax boundary on a nitrocellulose strip using a hot plate and a pipette tip.

substeps.instruction: Set the hot plate to 100ºC or a temperature sufficient to melt wax.
Place a small amount of wax from a wax pencil onto a Petri dish on the hot plate and wait for it to melt.
Cut a nitrocellulose sheet strip to the desired size.
Dip the broad end of a 200μL pipette tip into the melted wax, ensuring the whole circle contains enough wax.
Carefully place the tip onto the nitrocellulose strip, apply a little pressure, and remove the tip to leave a wax circle.

steps.title: Heat-treat the nitrocellulose strip
steps.instruction: Apply heat to ensure the wax penetrates through the entire thickness of the strip.

substeps.instruction: Sandwich the nitrocellulose strip between two sheets of paper.
Place the sandwich on the hot plate with a Petri dish (or any temperature-resistant flat object) on top to apply pressure.
Allow the strip to warm for 5 minutes.
Remove the strip from the hot plate and let it cool down.
Verify that the wax circle is present but the center remains clear.

steps.title: Apply streptavidin
steps.instruction: Add streptavidin to the center of the wax circle and dry.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of streptavidin (suspended in PBS without dilutions) onto the membrane.
Allow the protein to dry completely at room temperature.

steps.title: Block the membrane
steps.instruction: Apply blocking solution to the remaining empty spaces on the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of blocking solution (containing BSA, powder milk, and Tween 20) onto the membrane.
Allow the membrane to dry completely again.
